paragraphs.source_en: And the clay that fills your ears shall be pierced by those fingers that kneaded it. And you shall see.

paragraphs.source_en: After saying these things he looked about him, and he saw the pilot of his ship standing by the helm and gazing now at the full sails and now at the distance.

paragraphs.source_en: And these my mariners, who have heard the choir of the greater sea, they too have heard me patiently. Now they shall wait no longer.

paragraphs.source_en: The stream has reached the sea, and once more the great mother holds her son against her breast.

paragraphs.source_en: And if it suffices not, then again must we come together and together stretch our hands unto the giver.

paragraphs.source_en: A little while, a moment of rest upon the wind, and another woman shall bear me.

paragraphs.source_en: It was but yesterday we met in a dream. You have sung to me in my aloneness, and I of your longings have built a tower in the sky.

paragraphs.source_en: The noontide is upon us and our half waking has turned to fuller day, and we must part.

paragraphs.source_en: If in the twilight of memory we should meet once more, we shall speak again together and you shall sing to me a deeper song.

paragraphs.source_en: And if our hands should meet in another dream we shall build another tower in the sky.

paragraphs.source_en: So saying he made a signal to the seamen, and straightway they weighed anchor and cast the ship loose from its moorings, and they moved eastward.

paragraphs.source_en: And a cry came from the people as from a single heart, and it rose into the dusk and was carried out over the sea like a great trumpeting.

paragraphs.source_en: Only Almitra was silent, gazing after the ship until it had vanished into the mist.
